findings.issue: The comment on `reducedInvarDenom_zero` says `@[simp]` is omitted because "with the per-residue lemmas tagged, `simp` derives this ... and `simpNF` rejects the redundant annotation" — but `reducedInvarDenom_one` (line 257) and `reducedInvarDenom_two` (line 264) are tagged `@[simp]` and are proved by the identical bare `simp`, so simp derives them from `reducedInvarDenom_of_emod_eq_one`/`_two` just as much. summary: The main theorem's proof opens by stating and proving, as a local `have`, the general divisor-form complement lemma the module docstring says the repository lacks; it is one line from `normEDS_mul_complEDS` and is used nine times, so it belongs as a top-level theorem in `Complement.lean` rather than buried in a proof term. The module docstring's "No divisor-form lemma is involved" then contradicts the proof, and the `@[simp]` rationale on the three value lemmas contradicts itself.
